What the earlier sizing missed is that a tab's advance is POSITION-DEPENDENT, and every consumer of an advance is a prefix sum: `TextRun.Place` walks the shaped glyphs, `TextRun.CaretOffset` delegates to `ShapedText`, `TextRun.Width` is `Shaped.Advance * Scale`, and `LineWrapper` is handed a per-character array that cannot express 'this advance depends on where the line started'. Fixing the wrapper alone gives lines that break in the right place and draw in the wrong one, with the caret a tab-width out on any line holding one — the failure `text-transform` is split off to avoid. The clean seam is `TextLine`'s pen array, which already exists for mixed fonts and is what `PenOf`, `Place`, `CaretOffset` and `CaretIndexAt` are all expressed in terms of: split a run at each tab in `UiElement.Runs`, give `TextLine` a stop size and a per-run width override, suppress the tab run's glyph, and the four consumers follow. Plus the wrapper's position-dependent advances, which are circular (a tab's width depends on where its line starts, and where a line starts depends on widths) and want a first-fit pass that measures forward from each line's own origin.
